question: Which kind of emergency is imposed on the grounds of threat to the economic stability or credit of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial Emergency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Financial Emergency:**

 
 
• A Financial Emergency is imposed under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is declared when the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the central government can give directions to states to observe specified canons of financial propriety.
 
• Salaries and allowances of any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union and the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts can be reduced.
 
• It is designed to protect the economic stability of the nation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**President’s Rule:**

 
 
• President’s Rule is imposed under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is declared when the President is satisfied that the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It leads to the suspension of the state government and the imposition of direct rule by the central government.
 
• It is related to the breakdown of the constitutional machinery in a state.
 
• It is not related to financial stability.
 
 
 
• 
 
**National Emergency:**

 
 
• A National Emergency is imposed under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is declared when there is a threat to the security of India or any part of its territory due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It affects the fundamental rights of citizens and the distribution of powers between the center and the states.
 
• It is related to national security, not financial stability.
 
• This emergency has been declared several times in India's history.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Internal Emergency:**

 
 
• The term "Internal Emergency" is usually associated with the National Emergency declared in 1975, which was imposed on the grounds of "internal disturbance."
 
• This type of emergency is now covered under Article 352, which, after amendments, requires the threat to be due to "armed rebellion" rather than "internal disturbance."
 
• It is related to internal security, not directly to economic stability.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act of 1978, changed the wording of this section of the constitution.
 
• The emergency declared in 1975, is a very controversial part of Indian history.
